formationLabel: 1913 Urbonas parish/attempt and 1914 St. Peter lineage conflict · activity through 1919 and later relocation · terminal date unresolved
currentUse: The canonical route currently gathers conflicting evidence for one or possibly two Lithuanian independent or national Catholic efforts in Chicago's Town of Lake area. Michelsonas describes a parish founded by Rev. P. B. Urbonas in 1913 and lapsed after about two years. Wolkovich describes St. Peter the Apostle, founded by Rev. Zigmas Jankauskas in 1914 and served through 1919; Oikos says the 1913 attempt was unsuccessful and treats the 1914 St. Peter entry separately before reporting a later move to 1957 Canal Street and dissolution after several years. The original Town of Lake worship address, the directional prefix and parcel for 1957 Canal Street, all building outcomes, successor, and record custody remain unknown. No current congregation is asserted.
summary: This record represents a Lithuanian independent or national Catholic Town of Lake history that cannot yet be reduced to one certain founder, formation date, or end date. Michelsonas reports that Rev. P. B. Urbonas founded an independent parish in 1913 and that it lasted about two years. Wolkovich instead identifies St. Peter Parish, founded by Rev. Zigmas Jankauskas in 1914 and lasting through 1919. Oikos preserves both entries: its narrative calls Urbonas's 1913 effort unsuccessful, then says Jankauskas founded St. Peter the next year, served through 1919, and that the parish later moved to 1957 Canal Street in Chicago's 18th Lithuanian colony before dissolving after a few years. The existing crosswalk says the two readings are likely the same congregation but explicitly retains both; no charter, address, clergy succession, or continuity instrument resolves whether they were one congregation, successive phases, or distinct attempts. The inherited public closure of about 1915 is therefore too definite for the full canonical cluster. Both source lines describe historical cessation, but the exact identity, terminal date, formal PNCC relationship, sites, successor, records, and building fates remain unresolved.

institutionLifecycle.currentVerification: No current Town of Lake or 1957 Canal congregation, successor, parish archive, or record custodian was found. historicalNarrative.text: The canonical route concerns a Lithuanian independent or national Catholic effort in Chicago's Town of Lake area, not Holy Cross, St. George, Saints Peter and Paul, or another Roman Catholic Lithuanian parish. Michelsonas calls the institution Lithuanian National Catholic; Wolkovich calls St. Peter an independent/separatist Lithuanian Catholic congregation. The current canonical class is national_catholic_pncc, but the reviewed parish-specific sources do not supply a PNCC reception act or diocesan roster entry, so formal jurisdiction remains an explicit gap rather than an inferred fact.

historicalNarrative.text: Michelsonas reports that Rev. P. B. Urbonas founded an independent parish in Town of Lake in 1913 after earlier national-church work elsewhere and that the Chicago parish lasted only about two years. On that reading the institution lapsed around 1915. Michelsonas supplies no church name, street address, property, successor, or closure instrument, so the approximate end cannot be projected beyond the specific Urbonas account.

historicalNarrative.text: Wolkovich gives a different lineage: St. Peter Parish in the Town of Lake section was founded by Rev. Zigmas Jankauskas in 1914 and lasted through 1919. The Brain crosswalk labels the 1913/1914 difference a divergence, says the accounts are likely the same congregation, and instructs researchers to keep both. That crosswalk is a hypothesis, not evidence that Urbonas and Jankauskas led one legally continuous institution, and the later 1919 boundary directly conflicts with using about 1915 as the route's certain closure.

historicalNarrative.text: Oikos preserves the distinction more sharply. Its narrative says Urbonas tried to organize another national parish in Town of Lake in 1913 but that the attempt was unsuccessful; it then says Jankauskas arrived the next year, founded St. Peter the Apostle, and worked there through 1919. The accompanying parish table gives separate 1913 Urbonas and 1914 St. Peter/Jankauskas rows. This evidence does not prove two census institutions, but it prevents the dossier from silently treating one founder/date/end sequence as settled.

historicalNarrative.text: The St. Peter lineage later moved from Town of Lake to Chicago's 18th Lithuanian colony at 1957 Canal Street and dissolved after several years. The source supplies neither the transfer year nor a directional prefix, parcel, building description, or exact terminal year. The move is therefore recorded as a typed relocation relationship, not as proof that the 1913 Urbonas account continued to the Canal Street site or that a building transaction itself ended the parish.

historicalNarrative.text: No current congregation, successor, cemetery, record custodian, original Town of Lake address, or surviving worship building has been verified. The official Western Diocese PNCC site identifies the present diocese and its Chicago office at All Saints Cathedral but does not establish a connection to this historical route. The inherited public projection of founded 1913 and closed about 1915 captures only the Michelsonas reading; it must remain flagged until a separate identity and status adjudication determines whether the route represents one congregation, successive phases, or a conflated pair.

conflictsWithArchiveRecord: Michelsonas says Rev. P. B. Urbonas founded a Town of Lake parish in 1913 that lapsed after about two years. Wolkovich says Rev. Zigmas Jankauskas founded St. Peter in 1914 and served it through 1919. Oikos calls the Urbonas attempt unsuccessful, treats the 1914 St. Peter foundation separately, and records later relocation to 1957 Canal Street followed by dissolution after several years. Brain's crosswalk says likely same congregation but keep both; no direct evidence resolves whether these are one institution, successive phases, or distinct attempts. The inherited founded-1913/closed-about-1915 projection therefore overstates a single reading and cannot cover the 1914–1919 and post-relocation lineage. The national_catholic_pncc class is retained as protected canon, while formal parish-specific PNCC jurisdiction remains unverified.
gaps: No charter, incorporation filing, founding minutes, PNCC reception or assignment instrument, member or trustee list, complete clergy succession, original Town of Lake street address, church name for the Urbonas reading, deed, lease, directional prefix or parcel for 1957 Canal Street, dedication record, worship schedule, cemetery, sacramental register, exact relocation or dissolution year, closure act, successor, record-custody notice, demolition record, present ownership/current use, or structural/interior assessment has been found.
